description.narrative:
The expected project-level outcomes are: (i) Economy-wide Effects: by promoting local production of poultry meat, the Project is expected to contribute to increased value addition, employment creation and stimulate downstream linkages with related sectors. The Project will also create indirect jobs for MSMEs in the product value chains, and support import substitution; (ii) Stakeholder Consumer: the Project is expected to increase consumer access to affordable, safe and higher quality poultry products therefore contributing to food security in the country.
The expected market-level outcomes are resilience/competitiveness: the Project is expected to catalyze adoption of best practices that improve efficiency in operations and competitiveness of the market. The Project will also help supply Kyrgyz Republic with a reliable supply of affordable animal protein. The low volume of local poultry production has exposed the Kyrgyz Republics vulnerability to import restrictions from neighboring countries.

The proposed IFCs financing consists of a senior secured Kyrgyz Som (KGS)-denominated loan of up to US$20 million equivalent (the IFC Loan) to Adal Azyk LLC (AA or the Company), the largest sausage producer and integrated poultry farm in the Kyrgyz Republic, an IDA country, with about 55% market share in the fast-growing Kyrgyz sausage market, and a highly competitive position in the countrys poultry market. The IFC Loan will help fund the US$33 million investment program aimed at expansion of poultry operations in 2024-2026, including construction of 48 broiler sheds, and a new feed mill (the Project). The Project will be implemented by Agro Kush LLC (AK), a subsidiary of AA. The Project is expected to be supported by the IDA PSW Local Currency Facility (IDA PSW LCF) as described in the Blended Finance Section.
